title: Progressive Deceleration Entitlement Model and Billing Rules
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: High-level PRD for a progressive deceleration entitlement model intended to reduce customer-visible disruptions when tenants exceed soft quotas, while preserving predictable billing and clear invoice reconciliation. This feature introduces an entitlement tiering and deceleration policy that gracefully reduces throughput for low-priority routes, applies prorated overage charges, and auto-applies goodwill credits in repeat-first-occurrence scenarios.
background: Customers frequently prefer predictable, gradual degradation over immediate hard throttles when they breach quota. Existing soft-burst behavior provides transient buffer credits but lacks a standardized deceleration policy tied to billing controls and invoice clarity. This leads to ops escalations and manual bill adjustments. We need a repeatable model that ties runtime routing decisions (decelerate vs throttle) to billing rules and reconciliation logic.
goals: Define a server-side policy that transitions tenants from full throughput -> progressive deceleration -> hard throttle based on configurable thresholds
Create billing rules that translate deceleration events into prorated overage charges and automatic first-incident goodwill credits
Expose new console indicators and invoice line-items that make deceleration events auditable and easy to reconcile
Provide clear acceptance criteria and end-to-end tests for metering accuracy and invoice correctness
non_goals: Rewriting core token metering pipelines (we will integrate with existing metering systems)
Changing long-term subscription tiers or pricing bands (this PRD focuses on runtime & billing behavior for overages only)
Replacing existing burst credit mechanics entirely
requirements: Policy: Per-tenant soft_quota, decel_threshold (percent of soft_quota), hard_quota. Example default: soft_quota=100M tokens/month, decel_threshold=105%, hard_quota=120%

Runtime: When tenant usage crosses decel_threshold, mark subsequent requests for progressive deceleration for window W (configurable, default 10m). Deceleration should be route-aware and preferentially reduce throughput for routes labeled 'background' vs 'interactive'

Billing: Convert decelerated token consumption into overage_line_items at a reduced overage_rate (e.g., 0.75x standard overage) for first-occurrence in a billing period; subsequent occurrences billed at standard overage

Goodwill: If deceleration resolves without escalation within the period and this is tenant's first deceleration in 12 months, apply an automatic one-time credit equal to X% of the decelerated overage charge (configurable, default 100% up to $1000 cap)
Observability: Console must show deceleration timestamps, impacted routes, token counts attributed to deceleration, and the billing impact estimate prior to invoice generation
Metering accuracy: Token attribution for deceleration events must be >= 99.9% accuracy compared to authoritative ledger within 24 hours
Invoices: New invoice schema must include line items: base_quota_consumed, decelerated_tokens, deceleration_overage_rate, applied_goodwill_credit, net_overage_charge
APIs: Public usage API must surface an endpoint returning current soft_quota, decel_threshold, remaining_soft_tokens, and current deceleration_state
Admin controls: Support manual override to convert deceleration to hard throttle and vice versa for customer support agents with appropriate audit logs
edge_cases: Clock drift between metering systems causing temporary mismatch in deceleration attribution
Bursty traffic where a tenant oscillates across decel_threshold quickly (policy should include hysteresis to avoid flapping)
Multi-tenant shared pools where one tenant's deceleration decision affects autoscaling thresholds for the shared GPU pool
Customers using dedicated capacity with contractual hard limits—policy must be disabled for dedicated plans unless explicitly enabled in contract
acceptance_criteria: E2E: Under a synthetic load test that exceeds soft_quota by 10% sustained for 15 minutes, runtime should enter progressive deceleration within 60s and show decelerated_tokens >= 90% of expected in console

Billing: A generated test invoice should include deceleration_overage line item and an applied_goodwill_credit for first-occurrence tenants (test case with simulated first-occurrence) and net_overage_charge computed correctly
Metering: Reconciliation job compares runtime meter and billing ledger over a 24-hour window and reports >= 99.9% token parity for deceleration-attributed tokens
API: Usage API returns deceleration_state with correct remaining_soft_tokens during and after deceleration window
Console: UI shows deceleration events on tenant timeline with links to affected routes, and the cost impact preview matches invoice lines within 0.5%
Support: Manual override by a support agent is logged in audit trail and causes immediate change in behavior (deceleration->throttle or vice versa) within 30s
Regression: Feature toggles allow safe ramp to 100 tenants in staging before turning on for GA; all toggles respected and documented
implementation_notes: Runtime: Leverage existing per-tenant leaky-bucket rate limiter; add 'deceleration' state with configurable reduction_factor and hysteresis windows
Billing: Extend billing ingestion pipeline to accept 'decelerated_tokens' as a distinct meter stream; add pricing engine rule to apply reduced overage_rate and goodwill credit logic
Console: Add tenant timeline band for 'Deceleration events' and a cost preview modal that reuses the invoice simulator service
API: New endpoint /v1/usage/decels-status (internal-first) returning simple JSON; front-end should poll no faster than 30s to avoid additional load
Data: Add deceleration tag to existing token events (boolean flag) and ensure downstream ETL copies the flag into the billing warehouse
test_plan: Unit tests for deceleration state machine (hysteresis, thresholds, override behavior)
Integration tests: runtime + billing pipeline where decelerated tokens are emitted and ingested to billing ledger
E2E load tests in staging: run 10 tenants with mixed interactive/background routes to validate route-aware deceleration
Invoice snapshots: generate sample invoices for first-occurrence and repeat-occurrence tenants and compare line items to expected values
Canary rollout: Gradually enable for 10 beta customers and validate console metrics and invoice previews for one billing cycle
risks: Incorrect metering attribution could lead to customer disputes and refunds
Misconfiguration of reduction_factor could degrade UX for high-value interactive routes
Complex billing rules increase invoice generation time and failure modes in the billing pipeline
API surface increases operational load if polled aggressively by customers
